primary_antecedent.author: Lars Hörmander
primary_antecedent.title: The Analysis of Linear Partial Differential Operators III: Pseudo-Differential Operators
primary_antecedent.locator: Section 24.2, printed 423–424, especially (24.2.4); Section 24.7, Propositions 24.7.1 and 24.7.1-prime, printed 465–467.
primary_antecedent.receiving_contribution: An explicit uniform Dirichlet coercive estimate at strictly tangential-elliptic boundary covectors, with full localization, original Banach coarse control and one actual scalar source test.

source_correspondence: H0–H1 retain the full normalized scalar differential family, arbitrary complex lower terms, original Banach embedding, strict negative tangential principal form and fixed geometry before all orders. The conclusion includes bounded full targets and one fixed scalar source.

E0 constructs a positive tangential completion, proves coercivity by a full square factor with an order-one remainder and Fourier interpolation, and explicitly assembles the global inverse from compact-base charts and exterior constant Fourier multipliers.
E1 keeps the exact zero Dirichlet endpoint term and proves the weak source inequality for F+D_xG without differentiating a zero extension or assuming a trace of G.

E2 proves the exact sign in the exterior-derivative commutator, full outer-probe factorization and all residual bounds at the coarse order. One full derivative is gained without assuming the same normal derivative in advance.
E3 iterates the actual finite inequality with source indices s+j-2. The final target, collar, outer region and parameter neighborhood are independent of the number of gains.

S0 retains the actual gauged equation and trace. Coarse mixed regularity is derived from the original Banach norm and the complete admissible source tree, without a Banach multiplier-invariance assumption.

S1 writes the complete ratio-kernel source identity, moves the input normal derivative outside, and applies normal-cap ellipticity only on its valid transition band. Every full residual source branch is retained.
A0 recovers the original targets through a full tangential inverse and converts the residual acting on the gauged input back to an operator on u. The bounded auxiliary family is retained throughout.

A1 uses the already proved boundary-chart scalar assembly for the finite list. It removes the older whole-input product restriction without discarding forcing residuals or exceeding positive-dimensional halfspace scope.

G0 proves injective tested graph completion and states exactly when the limiting trace remains zero. Internal export closure, a general manifold adapter and the remaining all-regime observation theorem are unclaimed.

Three complete solutions verify the Dirichlet model energy, a complex normal gauge with positive residual potential, and exact cancellation by a nonzero boundary value. The original figure distinguishes symbol level sets from rays.
Formula and figure extents were measured on both viewports.
